_README: The committed LogHash determinism pin of M2-15 (`05` section 7).
WHAT THIS TABLE PROVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.
It proves STABILITY.  The encoding of a CombatEvent list -- field order,
widening, the enum ordinals, the element count, and the fact that log ORDER
is part of the hash -- cannot change without a row here going red.
It does NOT prove correctness of the encoding CHOICE against any external
authority, because there is none: nobody publishes `event list -> LogHash`
vectors for this game.  The rows below were produced by an independent
Python transcription of `14` section 16.6's encoding table and `05` section 7's
field list, and that generator first reproduced Landon Curt Noll's published
FNV-1a 64 vectors (the same set pinned in
Model/Snapshots/CanonicalStateWriterReferenceVectors.json).  So the HASH
FUNCTION is externally validated; the BYTES fed to it are pinned, not
published.  See steering rule S5.
Encoding, per `14` section 16.6 and the CanonicalStateWriter remarks:
root IReadOnlyList<CombatEvent> : 4-byte LE element count, then the elements
CombatEvent                     : a non-nullable value type -- NO presence byte --
then its six primary-constructor fields in order
int    Tick                   : sign-extended, 8 bytes LE
enum   Type                   : int-backed, sign-extended, 8 bytes LE
byte   SourceId               : zero-extended, 8 bytes LE
byte   TargetId               : zero-extended, 8 bytes LE
double Value                  : IEEE-754 bit pattern, 8 bytes LE
ushort DataId                 : zero-extended, 8 bytes LE
so one event is 48 bytes and a log of N events is 4 + 48N.
LogHash is a bare ulong, not a 'fnv1a:'-prefixed string: `05` section 7 types the
SimulationResult field as ulong and `11` section 6 compares the two sides
numerically.
Landon Curt Noll's published FNV-1a 64 vectors, re-asserted here so this file
is self-validating: the generator that produced the rows below reproduced
these first, and the writer under test is re-checked against them by
Fnv1a64KnownAnswerTests.  The input is raw UTF-8 bytes -- these are NOT
canonical-encoding rows and carry no length prefix.

rows.why: no events at all -- the 4-byte count alone, which is what stops an empty log hashing to the bare FNV offset basis
one BattleStart: the minimal real log, and the None sentinel in both actor slots
one Hit carrying a 4-dp damage figure -- the ordinary event
hero hits, then the enemy hits back
THE SAME TWO EVENTS IN THE OTHER ORDER -- `05` section 3.1 step 7 makes log order part of the replay, so this row must not share a hash with two-events-ordered
the same event twice -- without the count prefix this would collide with a one-event log under a naive concatenation
one event of each of the 18 CombatEventType members, in ordinal order -- this row is what pins every ordinal, so inserting a member mid-enum breaks it loudly

`18` section 2.5's sanctioned case: the Dicelord's Scramble queueing MODIFY_DIE_FACE. DataId is the battle-local effect index, Value the one runtime-resolved argument (the die face index), TargetId is None because the target is the RUN
`17` section 11's telegraph, 1.2 s (24 ticks) ahead of the mechanic it announces
the highest addressable actor id (254) against the None sentinel (255)
the last tick of the 90 s cap (`05` section 3: 1800 ticks)
a damage figure above 2^23, where a float carries no fractional digits at all -- the row that would collapse if Value were narrowed to float
SYS_ENRAGE firing at 1 Hz from 70 s: the first five of the twenty ticks the 90 s cap admits, so the log cost of the enrage is pinned rather than assumed
a negative Value -- the sign-extension path of the IEEE-754 bit pattern
